week.title: The Body Knows Before the Mind Does
week.subtitle: Cancer Season Opens · June 21

sun.note: Final days of Gemini — the mind at the edge of its season. Sun enters Cancer June 21 at the solstice, the longest day. The light tips toward the inner world.

moon.note: Moving through the week, pulling tides. Watch what emotions surface around the Full Moon in Capricorn June 21 — the solstice Full Moon is a rare and charged combination.

mercury.note: In Gemini, at home, in full voice. The messenger ruling its own season. Words come fast. Track which ones are true.

venus.note: Moving through Cancer, entering the domain of nourishment, roots, and belonging. What do you love that also holds you?

mars.note: In Taurus — slowed, deliberate, building. The warrior becomes the farmer. What are you cultivating with sustained effort?

jupiter.note: Exalted in Cancer through June 2026. The great benefic at maximum generosity. Abundance through emotional intelligence, family, and deep roots.

saturn.note: Conjunct Neptune in Aries — structure and dissolution still intertwined. What is real about your ambitions? What was illusion?

uranus.note: Early Gemini. The disruption of communication systems continues to unfold. Every transmission carries unexpected charge.

neptune.note: Conjunct Saturn. The collective dream in the decan of initiation. Vision and discipline negotiating at the root.

pluto.note: Retrograde in Aquarius. Collective transformation being metabolized inward. What power structure are you examining within yourself?

aspects.sun_moon: Solstice Full Moon — the two luminaries in opposition at the axis of the year. The peak of light meets the pull of deep water.
aspects.jupiter_saturn: Jupiter in Cancer trine Saturn in Aries — the great benefic and the great teacher in harmonious conversation. What you're building has long-term structure.
aspects.venus_jupiter: Venus applying to Jupiter in Cancer — a sweetness building in the home and the emotional body. What you love is growing.
aspects.saturn_neptune: Saturn conjunct Neptune — the ongoing dissolution of inherited forms. What must be released before the new structure can hold?

days.sub: Sun in late Gemini · Moon building toward Full

aspects.meaning: The mind is finishing its season. Take stock of what you said, named, and communicated in Gemini. The mouth is closing. The chest is opening.

aspects.planets: Moon waxing toward Full in Capricorn
aspects.meaning: Emotional volume rising. What responsibilities are you carrying? The Full Moon will illuminate what Capricorn rules in your chart.

aspects.planets: Moon in Sagittarius — fire, philosophy, long vision
aspects.meaning: The feeling body seeks meaning, distance, horizon. What do you believe that is actually true? What are you taking on faith that deserves examination?

aspects.planets: Jupiter exalted in Cancer — active all week
aspects.meaning: The great benefic continues its generous passage. The place in your chart where Cancer lives is being expanded, blessed, and asked to hold more.
The emotional body puts on its work clothes. What needs to be completed before the Full Moon illuminates it tomorrow? Finish what can be finished.
Structure and dissolution in the same breath. The forms you are releasing were never truly solid — they only felt that way. What remains when the mist clears is what was real.

days.sub: Summer Solstice · Full Moon in Capricorn · Sun enters Cancer

aspects.meaning: The longest day. Light at its maximum — and immediately beginning to turn inward. Cancer Season opens: the season of home, family, emotional intelligence, and the interior world. What does 'home' mean to you right now?

aspects.planets: Full Moon in Capricorn opposite Sun in Cancer
aspects.meaning: A Solstice Full Moon is rare and charged. The axis: what you feel (Cancer) versus what you must build (Capricorn). What emotional truth is the structure of your life unable to hold? This is what the Full Moon reveals.

aspects.planets: Jupiter in Cancer near the Full Moon axis
aspects.meaning: Jupiter amplifies the Full Moon's illumination. What is revealed is not small. What is expanded is not trivial. The blessing and the reckoning are the same event.

days.sub: Post-Full Moon · Sun in Cancer I

aspects.planets: Moon waning in Capricorn — beginning dissemination phase
aspects.meaning: What was revealed at the Full Moon is now being processed. Don't rush the integration. Capricorn Moon says: metabolize slowly, build from what you learned.

aspects.planets: Sun in Cancer Decan I — Moon-ruled
aspects.meaning: The first decan of Cancer is the most purely lunar. Feeling, nourishment, origin, memory. What is feeding you? What is it time to feed?
Emotional detachment as a gift. Step back from what the Full Moon surfaced. The pattern is clearer from distance.
The week's communications carry unexpected charge. Something you said or heard this week contained a disruption that will take time to understand.
The waning Moon in Aquarius is a natural time for solitude, reflection, and detachment from drama. Let the week settle.
What have you gathered this week — emotionally, relationally, materially? Cancer Venus wants to bring it home and hold it close.

calendar.title: Summer Solstice · June 21
calendar.body: The longest day of the year. In many traditions, a fire festival — Midsummer, Litha, the peak of solar power. Light at its maximum, beginning its turn toward dark. Not loss — completion. The full circle requires both arcs.

calendar.title: Full Moon in Capricorn · June 21
calendar.body: A Solstice Full Moon — the convergence of two of the most charged annual moments. Moon at 0° Capricorn opposite Sun at 0° Cancer. The axis of home and achievement, feeling and form, roots and peaks. What is the Full Moon showing you about the structure of your life?

calendar.title: Cancer Season Opens · June 21
calendar.body: The Sun moves into Cancer, the sign of the Moon. Emotional intelligence, family, ancestry, nourishment, and the inner world become the season's work. The mouth of Gemini closes. The chest of Cancer opens.

calendar.title: Fathers' Day · June 21
calendar.body: The Summer Solstice and Fathers' Day coincide this year. The Father principle and the solar maximum in one breath. Who are the fathers — literal and archetypal — that shaped your structure? What is yours to carry forward, and what is yours to release?

political.title: Solstice Full Moon and Collective Illumination
political.body: Full Moons in Capricorn tend to illuminate structures of power and governance — who has it, who doesn't, what holds and what falls. With Jupiter in Cancer amplifying the emotional response, the people's voice (Cancer) is louder than the institution's order (Capricorn) this week. Watch where those tensions surface publicly.

political.title: Mars in Taurus and Economic Reality
political.body: Mars in Taurus moves slowly, deliberately, and with attention to material reality. Economic questions — resources, land, labor, what things actually cost — are being worked on below the level of spectacle. The headlines may be elsewhere. The real work is in the ground.

political.title: Saturn-Neptune: The Ongoing Reckoning
political.body: Saturn conjunct Neptune continues its long transit through Aries. Structures built on illusion are still being tested. This includes political narratives, institutional authority, and national mythologies. What is being asked: what holds up under reality? What was always vapor?

symbols.title: The Solstice Point
symbols.body: 0° Cancer — the cardinal ingress of summer. In ancient sky-watching, the solstice was the hinge point of the year. The Sun stands still (sol-stice) before reversing. A moment of maximum and threshold simultaneously. Pause. You are at the hinge.

symbols.title: The Full Moon as Mirror
symbols.body: The Moon reflects sunlight. A Full Moon is the moment of maximum reflection — the inner world fully illuminated by the outer. Whatever the Solstice Full Moon shows you, it is showing you something the Sun has been building toward all Gemini season.

symbols.title: Cancer: The Shell and the Sea
symbols.body: Cancer's symbol is the crab — soft inside, armored outside. Moving sideways. Never approaching what it wants directly. The shell is not weakness. It is the wisdom of a creature that knows it is permeable. What are you protecting? What does the protection cost?

symbols.title: The Spiral
symbols.body: Cancer's motion is cyclical, not linear. The year spirals — we return to Solstice each year, but we are not the same person who stood here last June. The spiral allows repetition without sameness. What returned this year that is different from last year's version?

colors.title: Silver
colors.body: The color of the Moon. Reflective, luminous, containing all colors without asserting any. Cancer season calls for silver — worn, placed in the home, held in the hand. The Moon's metal, the metal of memory.

colors.title: Sea Green
colors.body: The color of shallow water, of the tidal zone — the space between land and sea, between the known and the unknown. Cancer lives in that in-between. Sea green at the threshold.

colors.title: Pearl White
colors.body: The iridescence of the oyster's interior — what is produced when irritation meets water meets time. The pearl is the Moon's jewel. Cancer's wisdom is often formed this way: something soft wrapping itself around something hard, over and over, until beauty results.

colors.title: Deep Indigo (Waning Moon)
colors.body: As the Moon wanes through the week, the color deepens toward indigo — the color of integration, the color of what happens when the light turns inward. The Full Moon is silver. The waning Moon is indigo.

herbs.title: Moonwort (Botrychium lunaria)
herbs.body: An ancient fern associated with the Moon across European folk traditions. Used in Midsummer rites. A plant of mystery, lunar timing, and the unseen. Rare and protected — honor it in awareness rather than harvest.

herbs.title: Lemon Balm (Melissa officinalis)
herbs.body: Melissa — the Greek word for honeybee. A calming, clarifying nervine ruled by the Moon. For the nervous system overwhelmed by Full Moon intensity. Drink as tea through the solstice week. The bees of the summer solstice visit this plant especially.

herbs.title: St. John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum)
herbs.body: The great Midsummer herb, traditionally harvested at the Summer Solstice when its yellow flowers are at peak. Named for the feast of St. John the Baptist (June 24). A solar herb harvested at the solar peak — captures maximum light and carries it as medicine through the darker months. For grief, nerve pain, and the literal storage of summer's light.

herbs.title: Elder Flower (Sambucus nigra)
herbs.body: Elder blooms at Midsummer, filling the air with cream-colored flowers and heady scent. A plant of the fairy world in British folk tradition — never cut elder without asking permission. Elderflower cordial, fritters, and tea at the solstice are ancient practice. The medicine: cooling in summer heat, supportive of the lymph and the immune system.

numerology.title: June 16 → 6
numerology.body: 1+6+6+2+0+2+6 = 23 → 5. The number 5 governs change, the body in motion, freedom, and the unexpected. Appropriate for a week containing the Solstice Full Moon. The 5 asks: what needs to shift?

numerology.title: June 21 (Solstice) → 3
numerology.body: 2+1+6+2+0+2+6 = 19 → 10 → 1. The number 1: beginnings, the self, initiation. Cancer Season opens on a 1 day. The new emotional cycle begins with the self at the center of it. Who are you in your feeling world? That question is the season.

numerology.title: Week Number 25 of 2026
numerology.body: 25 → 7. The number 7: inner knowing, spiritual vision, the examination of what is true beneath what appears. A 7 week asks for depth, not performance. This is a week for internal work, not external display — appropriate for a Solstice Full Moon that reveals what has been hidden.

tarot.title: The Chariot (VII) — Cancer's Major Arcana
tarot.body: The Chariot governs Cancer. A figure in armor — soft inside, armored outside — commanding two sphinxes pulling in opposite directions. The Chariot does not force the sphinxes to agree. It holds the tension between them and moves forward anyway. This week: what two opposing forces are you holding? The skill is not resolution. The skill is direction.

tarot.title: The Moon (XVIII) — Full Moon week
tarot.body: The Moon card rises with the Full Moon — the card of the unconscious, dreams, the things that surface from the depths that we didn't know were there. The Full Moon in Capricorn and the Moon card in Tarot share one message: what is shown in the night sky is what is true. Not comfortable. True.

tarot.title: 4 of Cups — Cancer Decan I (Sun this week)
tarot.body: The 4 of Cups: a figure sits under a tree, arms crossed, uninterested in three cups before them — a fourth appears from a cloud. Luxury becoming ennui. The gift unnoticed because the heart is elsewhere. Cancer Decan I asks: are you recognizing what is being offered to you? The fourth cup is already appearing.

moonNote: The Solstice Full Moon in Capricorn — June 21, 2026 — is one of the most charged lunations of the year. The Full Moon at the exact moment of the Sun's Cancer ingress means maximum light and maximum turn simultaneously. What is fully illuminated at the Solstice point is what you carry into the emotional season ahead.

decanNotes.sun: The Sun in Gemini III (if before June 21) or Cancer I (after June 21). The pivot of the year lives in this decan transition — the mind becoming the heart.
decanNotes.moon: The Moon's decan changes daily this week as it moves toward the Full Moon in Capricorn. Track where it lands in your chart.
decanNotes.mercury: Mercury in Gemini I–II: the messenger at home, at speed, in full native intelligence. The tongue knows what it's doing.
decanNotes.venus: Venus in Cancer I: the planet of love in the Moon-ruled decan. Nourishment, home, the body's need for care.
decanNotes.mars: Mars in Taurus I–II: the warrior in the body's sign. Slow, material, building something real.
decanNotes.jupiter: Jupiter in Cancer II: the great benefic in the Mercury-ruled decan of Cancer. Abundance through intelligent emotional navigation.
decanNotes.saturn: Saturn in Aries I–II: structure at the beginning of things. The form is still being determined.
decanNotes.uranus: Uranus in Gemini I: the revolutionary just entered the sign of language. Earliest possible placement — the disruption is brand new.
decanNotes.neptune: Neptune in Aries I: the dream at the beginning. Vision that has barely been born into form.
decanNotes.pluto: Pluto retrograde in Aquarius I: the transformation of collective systems turning inward. The interior revolution.
